content:
Quick answer: Alcohol may interact with medicines used for arthritis and can worsen some health problems. Ask your prescriber or pharmacist about your specific medication rather than assuming any amount is safe.

Why medicines matter

Methotrexate, pain medicines and other treatments have different cautions. Liver disease and other health conditions may change the advice. Check the patient information leaflet and discuss alcohol with your prescribing team.

Alcohol and symptoms

Alcohol is not a treatment for arthritis. Sleep disruption, dehydration and falls may make day-to-day symptom management harder. Gout can be triggered by alcohol in some people.

Practical steps

If you drink, consider alcohol-free days and keep within current UK low-risk drinking guidance. If you do not drink, there is no health reason to start. Seek individual advice before drinking while taking prescribed medicines.

When to seek help

Seek urgent medical advice for vomiting blood, black stools, severe abdominal pain or jaundice. Ask your GP or pharmacist for support if cutting down is difficult.
